label: Encoded origin-tolerance countermodel checked
description: With the origin interface restored (varied origins of one rigidly identified individual, origin-determined access, origin plenitude), every premise of ActualEuclidean.inertNecessaryConcrete except Euclidean access at actual holds while its conclusion fails, so the tolerance rival survives Arrival A in this encoding. The countermodel needs two individuals: the individual necessary relative to the witness world plus (b) must be absent from a successor of actual that plus does not see (aMinus), and the varied individual a is contingent. Group 2 records that the surrogate's own three-offset pattern with the varied individual restored at all offsets does not give a countermodel: that individual exists at every successor of actual. Model claims concern these finite interpretations only; whether a world may lack an actual individual (b at aMinus, a at bMinus) is permitted, not required, by the encoded commitments. Two individuals: any countermodel to Arrival A needs two, already forced by its premises (an individual necessary at the witness world and one contingent there); under the if-half, additionally the successor lacking the necessary individual must be cut off by a second individual's far origin. On a one-individual carrier the arrival's premises are unsatisfiable, so it holds there only vacuously. Scope (semantic challenge 2026-11-10): faithful only to the encoded origin-tolerance commitments (rigid identity; Salmon-style access iff shared individuals have near origins, whose if-half is OPEN; near-origin plenitude; one varied individual), with stipulated absences (a from bMinus and bPlus, b from aMinus) and a stipulated temporal profile not tied to origins; model-witnessed for this finite encoding only. Not tested: counterpart, vague or kind-relative tolerance, or recombination/deletion plenitude.

research_comparisons.conditions: Near is a tolerance, origin plenitude and a varied individual at actual hold together with reflexivity at actual, presence-to-existence, inert emptiness and the possible contingent-free past in Control.faithful.
research_comparisons.scope: Same Frame, Ontic and History carrier as ActualEuclidean.inertNecessaryConcrete; five worlds, two rigidly identified individuals, three origin offsets, natural-number times, selected world World.actual.
research_comparisons.coverage: One finite origin-tolerance encoding with rigid identity and a three-value origin space; not counterpart, vague-tolerance or kind-relative accounts, and not the possible-external-cause arrival.
research_comparisons.exclusivity: With the varied individual and near a tolerance, origin-determined access entails the negation of Euclidean access at actual (originToleranceNonEuclidean).
research_comparisons.witness: Control.faithful, group 1 of Control.Certificate (encoded commitments only, with stipulated absences and temporal profile); a is absent from bMinus and b from aMinus, so NecessaryConcreteAt fails at actual.
research_comparisons.next_step: Test whether the arrival's premises can be re-warranted to require an individual necessary at the witness world to exist at every successor of actual (a cross-world persistence bridge); or test externalNecessaryConcrete against Control.faithful.
